doc.title: Buddy Burns and Frank Pasley Interview, 1968-09-23

chapter: Kansas City, Chicago and California bands
title: Ory band lineup, Les Hite tour east, six years with Liggins
summary: With Hite from 1939 he went to New York and Boston until wartime, then spent about six years with Joe Liggins; he now plays only occasional gigs.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Piano player, yeah. Ed Garland on the bass, Minor Hall on the drums, Ory, and myself. I played up there with them for a long time. And then I left that and I went with Les Hyde, a big band.

That's 1939. We left here. He used to be at the Cotton Club here. We went to New York, Boston and all that. Stayed back there about two years until the war comes and the war starts taking so many musicians and we come back to California. And I played around here about a year. And then the next band I got with was Joe Liggins, Honeydresser. I stayed with him five years. Six years. All six.

Yeah. Outside of that I caught a few gigs and things. I mean I'm not very handy much, you know, I don't feel like running over the road too much now. You stopped playing now? Well, yeah, but I don't mean I don't practice, you know, still play. But outside of that, that's about the extent of it.
